promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Nov 1 2026, 8 weeks out, target under 3:45.

new.headline: Don't make up the missed miles. The heat and 5.5 hours of sleep cost you this week, not your fitness, so next week is a lighter 29 miles with one shorter threshold session and a 10-mile long run.

flags.title: Sessions came up short
flags.detail: Wed threshold stopped after 2 of 3 reps at 8:18/mi instead of 8:00. Thursday was missed, and the long run ended at 11 of 13 miles with two water stops. Heat and short sleep drove all three.

flags.title: Heart rate in the heat
flags.detail: easy runs averaged 151 bpm at 10:24/mi, against 138 bpm at 9:50/mi in cooler weeks. Run by effort and heart rate, not pace, until it cools down.

flags.title: Sleep and stress

flags.title: Right knee

answers.question: I missed Thursday and cut the long run short. Should I make up the miles next week?
answers.answer:
No, don't make up the miles. The missed work was lost to heat and short sleep, and adding it back would stack load on legs that are already tired.

| Session | Planned | Ran |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tue | 6 mi easy | 6.0 mi |
| Wed | 8 mi, 3 x 1.5 mi at 8:00/mi | 6.0 mi, 2 reps at 8:18/mi |
| Thu | 5 mi easy | missed |
| Sat | 4 mi easy | 4.0 mi |
| Sun | 13 mi long | 11.0 mi |
| Total | 36 mi | 27 mi |

Nine miles is not a hole in your build. The last five weeks ran between 24 and 35 miles, and one low week doesn't undo that. Next week is 29 miles, a little above what you ran and well below what was planned.

new.analysis:
The week points to heat and short sleep rather than lost fitness. Easy pace slowed by about 40 seconds a mile while heart rate rose 13 beats, and the Wednesday reps cost far more than the same session did on Aug 12. Your two threshold sessions in cooler weeks, at 7:59/mi with heart rates of 151 to 153, show the engine is where it was.

The zone numbers look poor for a simple reason. Only 11% of your time was in zones 1 and 2, but you didn't decide to run harder. The heat pushed easy runs into moderate effort, and that adds tiredness on top of the heat. Capping heart rate instead of chasing pace is what fixes it.

The plan itself asked a lot. It stepped from 24 miles to 36 in one week, straight after a week shortened by the knee, and then the heat arrived. With sleep at 5.5 hours, the real load was heavier than the miles suggest, so the shortfall is partly on the plan and not only on you.

Next week keeps the build moving without adding stress. One shorter threshold session holds the quality, and the long run drops to 10 miles so you can run it early and finish in better shape. Marathon-pace segments wait until the weather turns.

The race is still 8 weeks out, so there is time. If the AC is fixed and sleep recovers, the week of Sep 7 can take the long run back to 12 or 13 miles and bring marathon-pace work back. After that the job is stretching time on your feet toward 2.5 hours.

I would rather you skip a rep than run through a bad day. Under 8:35/mi marathon pace needs consistent weeks more than any single hard session.

settingsProposalBullets: Add that your right knee flared on the outside, worst on downhills, from Aug 13 to 16, and settled within a week with hip and glute work.
Add that you usually run early, around 6am, and heat is your main limiter right now.
Add that your easy runs sit near 138 – 140 bpm at about 9:50/mi in cool weather, so I can judge heat effects against that.
Add that your AC is broken until next week and work stress is high, which is cutting your sleep.

safetyCallouts.title: Running in the heat.
safetyCallouts.body: If you feel dizzy, nauseous, confused or get chills while running in the heat, stop, cool down and get medical help if it doesn't pass quickly. Two water stops and a heart rate far above normal mean heat is the limit, so slow down, start earlier or move indoors.

safetyCallouts.title: Tiredness that sticks around.
safetyCallouts.body: You feel tired all the time and your heart rate is high at easy effort. If that carries on a week or more after sleep and temperature improve, or you feel unwell, see a doctor before pushing training.
